 KLAS Las Vegas Follow Medicare Annual Open Enrollment with Southwest Medical, Part of Optum
 Mary Posey Tue, November 3, 2026 at 4:59 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Medicare Annual Open Enrollment with Southwest Medical, Part of Optum Medicare annual enrollment is underway and now's the time to review your coverage for the year ahead. Here with more from Southwest Medical, part of Optum Nevada, is Dr. Ismail.
 Why is this time of year so important for people? 
It happens once a year, right? And we're already in it and it ends on December 7th. So it's important to look at your benefits and your current coverage and realize whether this is what works for you next year. Just because it worked today or this year doesn't necessarily mean it's the same for next year.
 So you should constantly be evaluating what's coming up for the following year. 
Absolutely. Things change, your drug coverage changes, your costs change, out of pocket expenses change, it's important to get updated.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Tell us more about Optum and how all of this is tied together. 
Sure. We have plenty of clinics across the valley. We have primary care clinics, we have community centers, we have specialty clinics, urgent cares and we also offer telehealth via video and we have more than 350 providers across the valley.
 That is huge and telehealth is so big. What if someone skips this year? What happens then? 
So, remember, doing nothing is still doing something. You want to make sure you look at your current coverage and is it the right one for next year? So still look at it, speak with a licensed insurance agent and see if it's, maybe, it might be the right one, you might need to adjust it.
 Someone's watching right now. They're all jazzed about this whole thing right now. How does someone get started? What's the first step? 
Yeah, so if you don't already have a licensed insurance agent, make sure that - you need to know your needs first, right? So know what you need, know what coverages you need, know what prescriptions you have and you will be needing in the future and then speak with a licensed insurance agent.
 Okay. Any final steps that we should be looking at. 
Remember, December 7th is your deadline, it happens once a year and if you're not certain, you can always call our number.
 Advertisement Advertisement Okay, December 7th is the cut-off? Could someone take action on December 7th? 
Yeah, I hope you don't wait last minute, but yes you can.
 In other words, don't put it off.
